Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILC OPINION NO. 142 S. 2010 Atty. ANALYN T. MARCELO-BIJAN Director, Manila Barangay Bureau Office of the Mayor, City of Manila Dear Director Marcelo-Buan: This refers to your letter seeking our opinion as to whether or not Mr. Glicerio Bartolome is legally entitled to the benefits of the office of a Sangguniang barangay member from December l, 1997 up to the present. To recall, you represented that, during the 2007 Barangay Elections, Mr. Bartolome was among the candidates for the position of Sangguniang Barangay Member. However, he was proclaimed by the, COMELEC as elected barangay kagawad only on July 2, 2009. In the meantime, a certain Dionie Suing apparently took Mr. Bartolome's slot in the barangay council. Yet, Mr. Suing was not allowed by the punong barangay concerned to assume the post. Instead, it was Mr. Bartolome who has been performing the functions of said office since December l, 2007. With these, you now seek our opinion on the legality of Mr. Bartolome receiving the benefits of the office of a barangay kagawad since December I , 2007. Before responding thereto, we first take up the rules on the matter. First, settled is the rule that barangay officials are merely compensated by way of honoraria which are given for services actually rendered. This means that without any actual service rendered, the barangay official concerned is not entitled to the compensation due his office. Second, settled is the rule that the rightful incumbent of a public office may recover from an officer de facto the salary received by the latter during the time of his wrongful tenure [Monroy vs. Court of Appeals, 20 SCRA 620]. However, where there is no de jure officer, the officer de facto, who in good faith has had possession of the office and has discharged the duties pertaining thereto, is legally entitled to the emoluments of the office [Civil Liberties Union vs. Executive Secretary, 194 SCRA 317, Rodriguez vs. Tan, 91 Phil 724, Malaluan vs. COMELEC, G.R. No. 120193, March 6, 1996]. Accordingly, a de facto officer is one who actually and physically possess a valid existing public office under a color of title. There is a color of title to the office in any of the following cases: [al by reputation or acquiescence, the public, without inquiry, relies on the supposition that he is the public officer that he purports to be; [b] under a known and valid appointment or election but the officer failed to conform to a requirement imposed by law; [c] under a known

appointment or election but is void because of the ineligibility of the officer or want of authority of the appointing or electing authority or because of an irregularity in his appointment or election; or [d] under a known appointment or election pursuant to an unconstitutional law before the law is declared unconstitutional. [Antonio E.B. Nachura, Outline Reviewer in Political Law, 2009 Edition, pages 451-4531 In the instant query, we note that Mr. Bartolome has been performing the functions of the office of a barangay kagawad since December 2007. While his proclamation as elected barangay kagawad was made only on July 2, 2009, we are of the view that he may be considered a de facto barangay kagawad from December 2007 to July l, 2009. This is because, during said period, he actually and physically possessed the office of a barangay kagawad under a color of title thereto, that is, by reputation or acquiescence wherein the public had relied on the supposition that Mr. Bartolome was then a duly elected barangay kagawad. On the other hand, we note that Mr. Suing was the one proclaimed as elected barangay kagawad in December 2007 so that we are of the view that he was a de jure elected official until July 2, 2009 when his proclamation was nullified. However, we note further that no service was actually rendered by Mr. Suing because he was not allowed then by the punong barangay concerned to assume the post. As a consequence, he was not entitled to any compensation during that period. While, ck3ring the same period from December 2007 to July l. 2009, there was a de jure barangay kagawad in the person of Mr. Suing and a de facto one in the person of Mr. Bartolome, we opine that the latter is one entitled to the compensation due to the office of a barangay kagawad. This finds basis in the aforementioned rules that barangay officials are merely compensated by way of honoraria which are given for services actually rendered and that officer de facto, who in good faith has had possession of the office and has discharged the duties pertaining thereto, is legally entitled to the emoluments of the office. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Atty. JESUS B. DOQUE IV Director III 28 ccc GLICERIO BARTOLOME Barangay 135, First District City Of Manda ARD VIRGILIO A. CASTRO DILG-NCR
